title: Shortening the walk bound
statement: Let $E$ be a relation on the natural numbers and let $n,j,c,t\in\mathbb{N}$, with $c<n$ and $t<n$. If there is a walk from $c$ to $t$ of length at most $j$, then there is one of length at most $n$. A walk of length at most $j$ is defined recursively: at bound zero it means equality, and at a positive bound it means either equality or an initial step to some $v<n$ following $E$, followed by a walk with bound one less.
hypotheses_covered: there is a bounded walk from $c$ to $t$
